title: BIS Quarterly Review, December 2025
summary: The BIS Quarterly Review December 2025 provides comprehensive coverage of international banking and financial market developments, with major focus on FX and interest rate derivatives market structure based on the 2025 Triennial Survey. The publication examines shifting currents in derivatives markets, the cash-futures basis trade, and structural changes in global FX trading dynamics including hedging behaviors and liquidity conditions.
key_points: The 2025 BIS Triennial Survey provides detailed highlights on global FX and interest rate derivatives market structure and turnover
FX volumes surged notably in April 2025, with tariff news identified as a key driver of trading activity around that period
The cash-futures basis trade and exchange-traded interest rate derivatives positioning are analyzed in detail
Benchmark reform (Libor transition) is driving structural shifts in OTC interest rate derivatives markets
Geographical shifts in turnover include migration of euro contracts to Germany
Hedge funds' relative value trades in US Treasuries and interest rate swaps are sized up
Clearing concentration represents a structural challenge for emerging market OTC interest rate derivatives
Renminbi is propelling growth in emerging market currency trading
Non-visible FX trading and its relationship to liquidity conditions is examined
why_it_matters: The BIS Triennial Survey is the most comprehensive global study of FX and derivatives market structure, conducted every three years. This December 2025 edition captures structural changes post-Libor transition, the evolution of basis trading, and the impact of macro events (tariffs) on market microstructure. Market participants need this to understand current liquidity dynamics, hedging patterns, and the evolving role of different market participants.
macro_context: The publication contextualizes market structure developments within the broader macro environment, noting sovereign yield moderation with monetary easing, compressed credit spreads, and volatility challenges affecting risk-taking behavior globally.
market_structure_context: This is a market structure document. It covers: FX market microstructure and trading patterns; interest rate derivatives market structure and OTC-to-exchange migration; cash-futures basis dynamics; clearing concentration risks; the role of broker-dealers, electronic brokers, and voice brokers; and the impact of policy regimes (monetary tightening, benchmark reform) on market structure.
notes: This is a legitimate, high-trust source from the BIS (central bank of central banks). The publication is quarterly research (not a rate decision or data release).
